events.asset: Medicare NTAP for a psychedelic medicine (a psychedelic-class drug, or a therapy that administers one)
events.title: Medicare new technology add-on payment for a psychedelic medicine
events.proposition: CMS approves a Medicare new technology add-on payment (NTAP) for a psychedelic medicine (a psychedelic-class drug, or a therapy that administers one) in an inpatient prospective payment system final rule.
events.criterion: TRUE on the effective date (1 October of the fiscal year) of the Medicare inpatient prospective payment system (IPPS) final rule, published in the Federal Register by CMS, that approves a new technology add-on payment for a psychedelic-class drug (psilocybin, MDMA, LSD, DMT or a related compound) or for a therapy that administers one. An NTAP application, a proposed rule, a CPT code, an FDA approval, a Medicaid or commercial payer decision, or a payment for ketamine or esketamine does not count. Resolution source: the Federal Register, Medicare IPPS final rule, new technology add-on payment section. FALSE at the deadline when no such NTAP approval has been published.

resolution_source.name: Federal Register (Medicare IPPS final rule, new technology add-on payment section)

readings: 'this' = the Medicare new technology add-on payment (NTAP) mechanism that the post describes for SAINT; the event is written on that mechanism, not on any payment model in general.
'psychedelic medicine' = a psychedelic-class drug (psilocybin, MDMA, LSD, DMT and related compounds) or a therapy that administers one; ketamine and esketamine are not counted.
'paid for' = approval of the add-on payment in a final rule; an application or a proposed rule is not payment.

events.asset: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) devices, any manufacturer: a new authorized indication
events.title: FDA authorizes a TMS device for a new indication
events.proposition: The FDA grants a 510(k) clearance, De Novo authorization or PMA approval for a transcranial magnetic stimulation device for a disease or condition beyond those authorized for any TMS device at the statement date.
events.criterion: TRUE on the decision date in the FDA 510(k), De Novo or PMA database of a marketing authorization, dated after 2024-01-04, for a transcranial magnetic stimulation device whose indications-for-use statement names a disease or condition that no TMS device was authorized for on 2024-01-04. Conditions already authorized at the statement date (major depressive disorder including treatment-resistant depression, anxious depression, smoking cessation, obsessive-compulsive disorder, migraine for single-pulse TMS) do not count. A new population or protocol within an authorized condition, a breakthrough designation, an investigational device exemption or a non-US authorization does not count. Resolution source: the FDA 510(k) Premarket Notification database, with the De Novo and PMA databases for other pathways. FALSE at the deadline when no such authorization appears there.

resolution_source.name: FDA 510(k) Premarket Notification database; De Novo and PMA databases for other pathways

readings: 'indications' = FDA-authorized indications for use of TMS devices. The forecaster lists the four conditions he treats as current; they are the FDA-cleared psychiatric and addiction indications at the statement date.
'more indications' = at least one disease or condition new to TMS as a device class; one authorization for one new condition suffices. Any TMS manufacturer counts, since the forecaster names none.
A population expansion or a protocol change within an already authorized condition is not a new indication; a listed condition under another name (MDD for TRD) is not new.
The forecaster counts anxious depression as its own indication, so a new patient population for a listed disorder counts as a new indication.

events.title: PCN-101 (arketamine) development is discontinued
events.proposition: The sponsor of PCN-101 (arketamine) announces that clinical development of the program is discontinued.
events.criterion: TRUE on the date of the first definitive public statement by the sponsor of PCN-101 (atai Life Sciences, its subsidiary Perception Neuroscience, or a successor owner or licensee of the asset), in a press release, SEC filing or investor presentation, that development of PCN-101 (arketamine, R-ketamine) is discontinued or terminated, or that the program has been removed from the pipeline with no further development planned. resolution_source.name: atai Life Sciences press releases and SEC filings (EDGAR)

readings: 'The arketamine story is over' is read as the sponsor discontinuing the PCN-101 (arketamine) program, the only arketamine program in the post. The forecaster says this is unlikely.

events.asset: psychedelic medicines (class): REMS at FDA approval
events.title: REMS requirement on FDA-approved psychedelic medicines
events.proposition: Every psychedelic medicine the FDA approves carries a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) on its label at approval.
events.criterion: Resolved on the FDA REMS database (REMS@FDA) read together with Drugs@FDA. For each drug in the psychedelic class (MDMA or midomafetamine, psilocybin, ibogaine and any other compound its sponsor or the FDA describes as a psychedelic or an entactogen; esketamine and ketamine excluded) that receives FDA approval between the statement date and the item's deadline, check whether a REMS is in force on the approval date. FALSE on the date of the first such approval that has no REMS. TRUE at the deadline if every such approval carried a REMS. If no drug in the class is approved by the deadline, the condition is unmet and the item is void. Resolution source: REMS@FDA, with Drugs@FDA for the approval dates.

resolution_source.name: FDA REMS database (REMS@FDA), with Drugs@FDA for approval dates

readings: Psychedelic class: MDMA (midomafetamine), psilocybin, ibogaine, and any other compound its sponsor or the FDA describes as a psychedelic or an entactogen. Esketamine and ketamine are excluded: the author uses esketamine as the comparator, not as a member of the class.
'Come to market' reads as FDA approval; 'with one of these REMS on the FDA-label' reads as a REMS in force on the approval date.
'100%' is the share of the class, not a probability; the confidence phrase is 'will'.
